I implemented the eight operations in `list_ops.py` using pure recursion, per the spec's requirement to avoid existing functions (no `len`, `reversed`, `sum`, `list.append`, etc.):

- **`append`** — recursively prepends the first element of `list1` and recurses on the rest; returns `list2` when `list1` is empty.
- **`concat`** — flattens one level by appending each sublist to the concat of the remaining lists (so `[[[1],[2]], ...]` yields `[[1],[2], ...]`, matching the nested test).
- **`filter`** / **`map`** — recurse element by element, keeping/applying the predicate or function as appropriate.
- **`length`** — counts by recursion, returning 0 on the empty list.
- **`foldl`** — threads the accumulator left to right: `foldl(f, rest, f(acc, first))`.
- **`foldr`** — right-associative: `f(foldr(f, rest, acc), first)`, which correctly handles direction-dependent functions (e.g. the `el / acc` test expecting 9, and the string-concatenation test producing `"exercism!"`).
- **`reverse`** — recurses to the end, then prepends each element on the way back.

`list_ops_test.py` was left untouched and no new files were created.
